questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The unique opportunity to live and be a part of society in Central Asia - a part of the world, that i didn't knew much about before my exchange stay. It seemed like a great chance to go on adventure, when KIMEP University in Almaty showed up on the list of friendship universities with University of Copenhagen, and I thought that I had to grab that chance.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, and KIMEP University definitely made a great effort to do everything they could to inform about everything. I never stood in a situation where i didn't knew what to do when i arrived or in my first days in Almaty.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: KIMEP University provided transportation from the airport to the dormitory on campus, which was a great service, as it could be overwhelming to find way on your own, after arriving in a completely different country with different systems, valuta, language etc. KIMEP has a so-called International Office, that has been extremely helpfull. They have provided help whenever I needed it, and has when I arrived they helped me with logistics such as withdraw money, choose courses and get a Kazakh SIM-card.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It has been a great help and security that KIMEP have the International Office, as they have students that provides help every day.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A dormitory. You could choose between single room and shared room with one person.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A canteen that is open every day from 8AM - 17PM, and also kitchens on each of the four floors on the dormitory.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is a great way to meet new people, as you are always close to others. Also, a lot of chill and fun activities are going on - all voluntary stuff. To live in a campus also means that you are close to classrooms, which is extremely nice. Also, I have to say that the sleep-wake cycle is a little different here in Kazakhstan, as people in general are sleeping very late, which means that there is often noise until late in the night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was really simple, even though I felt a little lost in the proces after getting accepted by KIMEP University. I contacted a study guide who calmed me, and told me that it would all succeed in the end - which she was right about. It is pretty easy to go through the registration process at KU, even though it can seem unmanageable while you're in the process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Study guides and the "Selvbetjening" on KUnet.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that i wanted - 6/6. :-)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To relax when searching for registration before arrival in your exchange university - they are only interested in helping you, and it seems they often are able to get you into your first priorities when you arrive at the university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level has been extremely different from class to class - some has been really entertaining, educational and interesting. Other classes have been on a lower level, some really unstructured, others just unacademic. But still, I have learnt a lot from all classes

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of the courses has been really structured and theoretical, which i definitely like. These classes has learnt me a lot, and has a classic academic approach on teaching. Other courses has been unacademic and full of guesswork and undocumentated claims. Even though, these are also the courses that has provided me with the most new perspectives, as these professors seem to have a lot of opinions and attitudes. The level of my courses has variated a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Here at KIMEP University the freedom is way less than at KU. At KIMEP there is a absence politic, which means that you will fail a course if you have been absent for more than six classes. Also, students are continuously being tested at KIMEP. This includes 2x mid-terms, presentations in class and quizzed. The pedagogical approach is about the same, as professors are not really personally involved in the students -  still, you can always contact the professors if you need help or wants to inform them on anything.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Emerging Powers, Kazakh Spirituality, Terrorism and Security, Foreign Policy of Kazakhstan, Globalization and Diversity and History of Kazakhstan.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Foreign Policy of Kazakhhstan!!! Really interesting, and a very unique approach on foreign policy. Classes are extremely entertaining and informative. History of Kazakhstan is always recommendable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you want to cook yourself in the kitchen, you need to buy all the kitchen tools and cleaning stuff yourself. It is not very expensive in Kazakhstan, but still it is good to know.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation including taxis are really cheap, and the same are groceries.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At the dormitory fitness room are included, and so are a football- and basketball field and a café. There is also four TV-rooms.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are lots of clubs, including football, american football, basketball, table tennis, debate clubs, chess tournaments, music, movie nights.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend everyone to participate in sports or debate/chess/music clubs. It is a great way into a community.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just to walk around Almaty, and to visit Medeu/Shymbulak in the mountains - it is only 25 minutes in taxi. In Alamty you can find lots of good and cheap restaurants, a great bazar and Arasan which is a popular sauna. Also, you should visit Astana if you want to experience a completely different, futuristic and cheap city. Kyrgyzstan is definitely worth a trip, but a weekend is not enough - I would recommend to visit in holidays. Uzbekistan is also great and really interesting.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy - people are interested and open for foreigners.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just say hallo and all the rest will happen if you want it to. The Kazakhs are so friendly and curious.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing was challenging, only interesting.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and calmly behaviour that I have experienced in all of the Central Asian countries.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. All the practical stuff will be solved, even though it sometimes seems hopeless. KIMEP offers such a great service, and things will settle down when you arrive.
2. Be prepared that Kazakhstan doesn't have an embassy in Denmark, and vice versa. This means that you have to go to Stockholm to get your Kazakh visa. This can be a little challenging and frustrating if you dont know.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: KIMEP is extremely inspired by American universities when it comes to expression and culture, but still it provides you with great knowledge and insight in Central Asia. All classes are in English, and student life is full of great offers.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The way I was welcomed by the Kazakh students and the university. This made the foundation for me to get to know people and the culture. Also, the fantastic travels was very rewarding. I have seen people and culture that I knew nothing about before.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I sometimes missed Denmark. Things are very different over here. But only in a good way!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I am extremely grateful that I had the opportunity to go on exchange. It has opened my eyes for Central Asia, and means that I have met many fantastic people and have had great experiences.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
